## **Previously on 201: Set Theory**
<br>
.pull-left[
1. in a set, **order** of items <span style="color:green"><b>does not</b></span> matter
  - {a, b, c} = {a, c, b} = {b, a, c} = {b, c, a} = {c, a, b} = {c, b, a} 
<br><br>
2. **repetitions** of items <span style="color:green"><b>do not</b></span> matter
  - {a, b, c} = {a, a, a, b, c} = {a, b, b, c, c}
<br><br>
3. an <span style="color:green"><b>item</b></span> in a set is called the **MEMEBER** of that set
  - and we use symbol **∈** to describe membership relation <br><br>
  - a **∈** {a, b, c}
  - a **is in** / <span style="color:green"><b>belongs to</b></span> / <span style="color:blue"><b>is an element of</b></span> the set {a, b, c}
]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1028/natural.jpg" width="70%">
</div>
]

### **∈ ∉**

## **Previously on 201: Set Theory**
.pull-left[
### **list notation**
<br>
the **list notation** specifies a set by <span style="color:green">listing its members</span>  between {curly brackets}<br><br>
  - The set <span style="color:green">*T*</span> is characters in ***Tom and Jerry***
  - <span style="color:green">*T*</span> = {Tom, Jerry, Tuffy, Spike, Tyke, Butch, Quacker, Cuckoo...}
<br><br>
<div style="text-align:center;">
<img src="../pic/1028/tom.gif" width="20%"><img src="../pic/1028/jerry.gif" width="20%"><img src="../pic/1028/spike.gif" width="20%"><img src="../pic/1028/tyke.gif" width="20%">
</div>
<br>

### **venn diagram notation**
]

.pull-right[
### **predicate notation**
<br>
The **predicate notation** specifies a set by <span style="color:green">describing member's property</span><br><br>
- <span style="color:green">*S*</span> = { x **|** x is a sorcerer }
- "<span style="color:green">*S*</span> equals the set of elements <span style="color:blue"><b>*x*</b></span>, such that **every** <span style="color:blue"><b>*x*</b></span> is a sorcerer"
- normal words: "the set of all sorcerers"
- **|** stands for "*<u>such that</u>*" 
<br><br>
<div style="text-align:center;">
  <img src="../pic/1028/sor.gif" width="25%">
</div>
]

## **Previously on 201: Set Relations**
<br>
.pull-left[
### **cardinality**: the number of elements in a set
<br>
- if A = {a, b, c}

  then the **cardinality** of the set A, **|A|** = 3
  
  also, **|A|** = **| {a, b, c} |**<br><br>
- <span style="color:green"><b>singleton set</b></span>: a set with cardinality = 1
- <span style="color:green"><b>null set</b></span> <span style="color:green"><b>empty set</b></span>: a set with cardinality = 0
  - {} = **Ø** "empty set"
]

.pull-right[
### **subset (⊆)**
*A* is a subset of *B* if **every** element of *A* is **also** an element of *B*

.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center;">
{a, b} **⊆** {a, b, c}
</div>]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center;">
{a, b} **⊆** {a, b}
</div>]<br><br>

- a ⊆ {a, b, c} is <b>WRONG</b>, why?<br>

<h3><span style="color:green"><b>proper subset (⊂)</b></span></h3>
<i>A</i> is a proper subset of <i>B</i> if <i>A</i> is a <span style="color:green"><b>subset</b></span> of <i>B</i> and they are not <span style="color:green"><b>identical</b></span><br>

.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center;">
{a, b} <span style="color:green"><b>⊂</b></span> {a, b, c}
</div>]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center;">
{a, b, c} <span style="color:green"><b>⊄</b></span>  {a, b}
</div>]<br>

### <span style="color:blue"><b>identity (=)</b></span>
- two sets are identical/equal if they have <span style="color:blue"><b>exactly the same elements</b></span>
  - {a, b} <span style="color:blue"><b>=</b></span> {b, a}
]

## **Previously on 201: Set Relations in Languages**
<br><br>
.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:deeppink"><i>Snoopy runs</i>.</span></b></h3>
</div>
]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:deeppink"><i>Cats run</i>.</span></b></h3>
</div>
]
<br><br><br><br>
.pull-left[
- <i><u>Snoopy runs</u></i>. has the form **Name VERBS**<br><br>
  - [[Snoopy]] = **element** Snoopy = s<br><br><br><br>
  
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:green">[[Snoppy]] ∈ [[run]]</span></b></h3>
</div>
]
.pull-right[
- <i><u>cats run</u></i>. has the form **NOUNs VERB**<br><br>
  - [[cat]] = **set** of all cats = { x | x is a cat }<br><br><br><br>

<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:green">[[cat]] ⊆ [[run]]</span></b></h3>
</div>
]

## **Compositional Semantics: NPs**
<br>
- suppose I wanted to use an **NP** like <u><i>yellow birds</i></u>
<br><br>
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:green"><i>What kind of birds do you like</i>?</span></b></h3>
<h3><b><span style="color:orange"><i>Yellow birds</i>!</span></b></h3>
</div>
<br><br>

- by using this **NP**, we are not making a <b><span style="color:blue">claim</span></b><br><br>
- we did not say "<u><i>birds are yellow</i></u>"<br><br>
- we are just trying to refer to **all elements** that are **simultaneously** in both [[bird]] and [[yellow]]<br><br>
- to define this in set theory, we need **set operations**

---
## **Set Operations**
<br>
- **set operations** are ways of taking <b><span style="color:green">existing sets</span></b> and creating a <b><span style="color:blue">new set</span></b> out of them<br>
  this is analogous to how **addition** and **subtraction** take <b>two</b> numbers and make a <b>third</b> number<br><br>
- four set operations: **union (∪)**, <b><span style="color:green">intersection (∩)</span></b>, <b><span style="color:blue">difference (–)</span></b>, <b><span style="color:deeppink">complement (')</span></b><br><br><br><br>

.pull-left[
imagine a **universe ** <b>U</b>, in that universe, there are five elements divided into two **sets**<br><br>
  - let A = { x ∈ U | x is an animal } = { rabbit, chicken, frog }<br><br>
  - let B = { x ∈ U | x is green } = { tree, frog, pepper }<br><br>
  - notice that **frog** is in both A and B
]
.pull-right[
<img src="../pic/1028/setop1.png" width="100%">
]



---
## **Set Operations: Union**
<br>
**union** of A and B produces a new set, which contains all **elements** that **belong to A or B** (or both).
  - A **∪** B = { rabbit, chicken, frog, tree, pepper }
<br><br><br><br>
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1028/setop2.png" width="60%">
</div>

---
## **Set Operations: Intersection**
<br>
<b><span style="color:green">intersection</span></b> of A and B produces a new set that contains all elements that **belong to both A and B**
  - A <b><span style="color:green">∩</span></b> B = { frog }
  - <b><span style="color:green">intersection</span></b> is the part that **overlaps** between two sets in a Venn diagram
<br><br><br>
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1028/setop3.png" width="60%">
</div>

---
## **Set Operations: Difference**
<br>
<b><span style="color:blue">difference (–)</span></b> of A and B produces a new set, which contains all elements that **belong to A but not B**
  - A <b><span style="color:blue">–</span></b> B = { rabbit, chicken }
  - **note** that A <b><span style="color:blue">–</span></b> B **≠** B <b><span style="color:blue">–</span></b> A
<br><br><br><br>
.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center">
A <b><span style="color:blue">–</span></b> B<br><br>
<img src="../pic/1028/setop4.png" width="100%">
</div>
]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
B <b><span style="color:blue">–</span></b> A<br><br>
<img src="../pic/1028/setop5.png" width="100%">
</div>
]

---
## **Set Operations: Complement**
<br>
<b><span style="color:deeppink">complement</span></b> of A produces a new set, which contains all elements **in the specified universe (U) that are not in A**
  - A<b><span style="color:deeppink">'</span></b> = { tree, pepper }
  - the symbol of <b><span style="color:deeppink">complement</span></b>  is tiny, so be careful
<br><br><br>
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1028/setop6.png" width="60%">
</div>

---
## **Set Operations: Summary**
<br>
<table style="width:100%; border-collapse: collapse;">
  <tr>
    <td style="width:25%; padding: 20px;"><b><span style="color:#CC0033">union (∪)</span></b></td>
    <td style="width:50%; padding: 20px;">
      <div><i>A ∪ B = { x ∈ U | x ∈ A or x ∈ B }</i></div>
      <div style="margin-top:10px;">(elements in A or B or <i>both</i>)</div>
    </td>
    <td style="width:20%; padding: 20px; text-align:center;">
      <img src="../pic/1028/setop2.png" width="80%">
    </td>
  </tr>

  <tr>
    <td style="padding: 20px;"><b><span style="color:green">intersection (∩)</span></b></td>
    <td style="padding: 20px;">
      <div><i>A ∩ B = { x ∈ U | x ∈ A and x ∈ B }</i></div>
      <div style="margin-top:10px;">(elements in both A and B)</div>
    </td>
    <td style="padding: 20px; text-align:center;">
      <img src="../pic/1028/setop3.png" width="80%">
    </td>
  </tr>

  <tr>
    <td style="padding: 20px;"><b><span style="color:blue">difference (–)</span></b></td>
    <td style="padding: 20px;">
      <div><i>A − B = { x ∈ U | x ∈ A and x ∉ B }</i></div>
      <div style="margin-top:10px;">(elements in A but not B)</div>
    </td>
    <td style="padding: 20px; text-align:center;">
      <img src="../pic/1028/setop4.png" width="80%">
    </td>
  </tr>

  <tr>
    <td style="padding: 20px;"><b><span style="color:deeppink">complement (')</span></b></td>
    <td style="padding: 20px;">
      <div><i>A' = { x ∈ U | x ∉ A }</i></div>
      <div style="margin-top:10px;">(elements in U but not A)</div>
    </td>
    <td style="padding: 20px; text-align:center;">
      <img src="../pic/1028/setop6.png" width="80%">
    </td>
  </tr>

</table>

.pull-left[

2. A – B<br>
  <span style="color:white">- <b><span style="color:white">difference</span></b>: {apple, plum}</span><br><br>
3. B ∩ C<br>
  <span style="color:white">- <b><span style="color:white">intersection</span></b>: {orange}</span><br><br>
4. B ∩ D<br>
  <span style="color:white">- <b><span style="color:white">intersection</span></b>: Ø or {}</span><br><br>

## **Set Operations in Natural Languages**
<br>
.pull-left[
- returning to our **NP** <span style="color:green"><b>yellow birds</b></span>:<br><br>
  - <span style="color:green">[[yellow birds]]</span> refers to **all elements** that are in both <span style="color:deeppink">[[yellow]]</span> and <span style="color:blue">[[bird]]</span>
  - simultaneously in two sets<br><br>
- what **set operation** do we use to specify elements that are **simultaneously** in two sets?<br><br>
  - intersection (∩): A **∩** B = all elements that are in both A and B at the same time
  - <span style="color:deeppink">[[yellow]]</span> **∩** <span style="color:blue">[[bird]]</span> = all elements that are in both [[yellow]] and [[bird]] = [[yellow bird]]<br><br>
- any **NP** of type <u>ADJ NOUN</u> can be specified in set theory via **intersection**: [[ADJ]] **∩** [[NOUN]]
]
.pull-right[
<br>
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1028/yellowbird.png" width="90%">
</div>
]
---
## **Set Operations in Natural Languages**
<br>
.pull-left[
- this **NP** <span style="color:green"><b>yellow birds</b></span> is further usable in structures we've already seen<br><br>

.pull-left[
<i>Tweety is a <span style="color:deeppink">bird</span></i>.
]
.pull-right[
[[Tweety]] **∈** [[bird]]
]
<i>Tweety is a <span style="color:blue">yellow</span> <span style="color:deeppink">bird</span></i>.<br>
<div style="text-align:right">
[[Tweety]] **∈** [[yellow]] **∩** [[bird]]
</div><br>

.pull-left[
<i><span style="color:blue">Birds</span> are pretty</i>.]
.pull-right[
[[bird]] **⊆** [[pretty]]
]
<i><span style="color:deeppink">Yellow</span> <span style="color:blue">birds</span> are pretty</i>.<br>
<div style="text-align:right">
[[yellow]] **∩** [[bird]] **⊆** [[pretty]]
</div><br>

- again, this demonstrates the **Principle of Semantic Compositionality**<br><br>
- more complicated sentences usually need more composing and more set relations

]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1028/yellowbird.png" width="80%">
</div>
<br>
- note that set operators (∪, ∩, −, ′) **take precedence over** set relation symbols (∈, ⊆, =)
- compare this to arithmetic operators (+, –, ×, ÷) and (in)equality symbols (=, <, >) in algebra
]

---
## **Set Theory in Semantics So Far**
<br>
.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1028/setoperation.jpg" width="70%">
</div>
]
.pull-right[
- we can define words by **reference** – the set of things they refer to<br><br>
- we can use set theory to precisely define the reference of a **natural language expression**<br><br>
  - **sets** are **collections** of elements<br><br>
  - **set relations** can capture the relationship **between words**<br>
  <u><i>Cats are mammals</u></i>.(hypo/hypernyms)<br>
  <u><i>Snoopy is happy</u></i>.(declarative sentences)<br><br>
  - **set operations** can capture the reference of **NP**s like ADJ NOUN<br><br>
- at last, we use**cardinality** to define **quantifiers**
]

## **Semantics of Determiners**
<br>
.pull-left[
<br>
  <img src="../pic/1028/the.jpg" width="100%">
]
.pull-right[
- we previously defined **determiner** as a part of speech and it consists of<br><br>
  <small>
  - <span style="color:deeppink"><b>articles</b></span> – <i>the</i>, <i>a</i>
  - <span style="color:green"><b>demonstratives</b></span> – <i>this</i>, <i>that</i>, <i>these</i>, <i>those</i>
  - <span style="color:#CC0033">q<b>uantifiers</b></span> – <i>every</i>, <i>some</i>, <i>many</i>, <i>most</i>, <i>no</i>
  - <span style="color:blue"><b>possessive pronouns</b></span> – <i>my</i>, <i>your</i>, <i>her</i>, <i>his</i>, <i>their</i>, <i>our</i>
  - some <span style="color:orange"><b>question words</b></span> – <i>which</i>, <i>what</i>  </small><br><br>
- determiners serve to **specify** which member of a set we're **referring to** in the world<br><br>
  <small>
  - <i><span style="color:blue"><b>my</b></span> dog</i> – a **member** of [[dog]] that belongs to me
  - <i><span style="color:green"><b>this</b></span> dog</i> – a **member** of [[dog]] that is near me
  - <i><span style="color:#CC0033"><b>every</b></span> dog</i> – the **entire set** of [[dog]]
  - <i><span style="color:deeppink"><b>the</b></span> dog</i> – a **member** of [[dog]] that is relevant to our current conversation
  - <i><span style="color:deeppink"><b>a</b></span> dog</i> – an unspecified **member** of [[dog]]
  </small>
]

---
## **Semantics of Quantifiers**
<br>
.pull-left[
- **quantifiers** (including numerals) are specific type of **determiners** that describes how many **members** of a set we're talking about<br><br>

.pull-left[
1. <span style="color:green"><b>every</b></span> cat<br><br>
2. <span style="color:green"><b>some</b></span> cats<br><br>
3. <span style="color:green"><b>three</b></span> cats<br><br>
4. <span style="color:green"><b>many</b></span> cats<br><br>
5. <span style="color:green"><b>most</b></span> cats<br><br>
6. <span style="color:green"><b>no</b></span> cats
]
.pull-right[

]
]

.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1028/forall.jpeg" width="80%">
</div>
]

---
## **Semantics of Quantifiers**
<br>
.pull-left[
- **quantifiers** (including numerals) are specific type of **determiners** that describes how many **members** of a set we're talking about<br><br>

.pull-left[
1. <span style="color:green"><b>every</b></span> cat<br><br>
2. <span style="color:green"><b>some</b></span> cats<br><br>
3. <span style="color:green"><b>three</b></span> cats<br><br>
4. <span style="color:green"><b>many</b></span> cats<br><br>
5. <span style="color:green"><b>most</b></span> cats<br><br>
6. <span style="color:green"><b>no</b></span> cats
]
.pull-right[
all<br><br>
more than zero<br><br>
exactly three<br><br>
a large number<br><br>
more than half<br><br>
zero
]
]

.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
<img src="../pic/1028/forall.jpeg" width="80%">
</div>
]

## **Semantics of Quantifiers**
<br>
- **declarative sentences** like <span style="color:blue">NOUNs are NOUNs</span>, <span style="color:blue">NOUNs are ADJ</span>, or <span style="color:blue">NOUN VERBs</span> make some **claim** about the relationship between sets<br>
.pull-left[
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:deeppink"><i>Cats run</i>.</span></b></h3>
⬇
<h3><b><span style="color:green">[[cat]] ⊆ [[run]]</span></b></h3>
</div>
]
.pull-right[
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:deeppink"><i>Snoopy runs</i>.</span></b></h3>
⬇
<h3><b><span style="color:green">[[Snoppy]] ∈ [[run]]</span></b></h3>
</div>
]
<br><br>
- sentences with **quantifiers** like <span style="color:blue">QUANT NOUN VERBs</span> also make some **claim** about the relationship between sets – but now it involves some **quantity**<br>
<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:blue"><i>Four cats are running</i>.</span></b></h3>
</div>

  - how many elements are <span style="color:#CC0033"><b>both</b></span> in <span style="color:deeppink">[[cat]]</span> and <span style="color:deeppink">[[run]]</span>?
  - the **cardinality** of the intersection of <span style="color:deeppink">[[cat]]</span> and <span style="color:deeppink">[[run]]</span> is <span style="color:blue"><b>four</b></span>, in other words, there are <span style="color:blue"><b>exactly four elements</b></span> that are both in <span style="color:deeppink">[[cat]]</span> and <span style="color:deeppink">[[run]]</span>

--

<div style="text-align:center">
<h3><b><span style="color:#CC0033">| [[cat]] ∩ [[run]] | = 4</span></b></h3>
</div>

## **Semantics of Quantifiers**
<br>
<div style="padding-left: 25px; padding-right: 25px;">

<table style="width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; table-layout: fixed;">
  <colgroup>
    <col style="width: 20%;">
    <col style="width: 30%;">
    <col style="width: 25%;">
    <col style="width: 25%;">
  </colgroup>

  <tr>
    <td><b>quantifier</b></td>
    <td><b>example</b></td>
    <td colspan="2"><b>set theory expression</b> (| [[N]] ∩ [[VP]] | = ?)</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style="color:white">-</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style="color:white">-</td>
  </tr>

  <tr>
    <td><span style="color:green"><b>numeral</b></span> N VP</td>
    <td><i><span style="color:blue"><b>Two</b></span> students run</i>.</td>
    <td>| [[N]] ∩ [[VP]] | <span style="color:#CC0033">= n</span></td>
    <td style="text-align:right">(n specificed by numeral)</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style="color:white">-</td>
  </tr>

  <tr>
    <td><span style="color:green"><b>some</b></span> N VP</td>
    <td><i><span style="color:blue"><b>Some</b></span> students run</i>.</td>
    <td style="color:white">| [[N]] ∩ [[VP]] | <span style="color:white">≠ 0</span></td>
    <td style="text-align:right; color:white"><b>or</b> [[N]] ∩ [[VP]] <span style="color:white">≠ Ø</span></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style="color:white">-</td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td><span style="color:green"><b>every</b></span> N VP</td>
    <td><i><span style="color:blue"><b>Every</b></span> student runs</i>.</td>
    <td style="color:white">| [[N]] ∩ [[VP]] | <span style="color:white">= | [[N]] |</span></td>
    <td style="text-align:right; color:white"><b>or</b> [[N]] ⊆ [[VP]] = <span style="color:white">TRUE</span></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style="color:white">-</td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td><span style="color:green"><b>many</b></span> N VP</td>
    <td><i><span style="color:blue"><b>Many</b></span> students run</i>.</td>
    <td style="color:white">| [[N]] ∩ [[VP]] | <span style="color:white">> n</span></td>
    <td style="text-align:right; color:white">(n is some large number)</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style="color:white">-</td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td><span style="color:green"><b>most</b></span> N VP</td>
    <td><i><span style="color:blue"><b>Most</b></span> students run</i>.</td>
    <td colspan="2"; style="color:white">| [[N]] ∩ [[VP]] | <span style="color:white">>  ½ | [[N]] |</span></td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td style="color:white">-</td>
  </tr>
  
  <tr>
    <td><span style="color:green"><b>no</b></span> N VP</td>
    <td><i><span style="color:blue"><b>No</b></span> students run</i>.</td>
    <td style="color:white">| [[N]] ∩ [[VP]] | <span style="color:white">= 0</span></td>
    <td style="text-align:right; color:white"><b>or</b> [[N]] ∩ [[VP]] <span style="color:white">= Ø</span></td>
  </tr>

</table>
</div>

## **Limitations of Set Theory**
<br>
- so set theory is a useful way to be **precise** about the **semantic meaning** of language<br><br>
- yet, there are a few things that **cannot** be described in set theory<br><br>
- an example is **non-intersective** adjectives<br><br>
  - an adjective like yellow in yellow bird is called **intersective** because <span style="color:green">[[yellow bird]]</span> can be described as the **intersection** between <span style="color:deeppink">[[yellow]]</span> and <span style="color:blue">[[bird]]</span><br><br>
  - what about <u><i>biggest tree</i></u> or <u><i>matching shirts</i></u>?<br><br>
  - we need more information – for instance to know which tree is biggest, we need to know the size of all other trees we need to compare them<br><br>
- also, we have not yet differentiated pairs like <u><i>Cats run</i>.</u> and <u><i>Cats are running</i>.</u><br><br>
- so **set theory** IS useful, but it **CANNOT** describe all aspects of semantics

**N** = { x | x is a human} = {Mario, Luigi, Baby Mario, Baby Luigi, Peach, Daisy, Wario, Waluigi}<br>

]
.pull-right[

<br>
.pull-left[
<small>
A **=** B: equality/identity<br>
A **⊆** B: subset<br>
A **⊂** B: proper subset
</small>
]
.pull-right[
<small>
A **≠** B: not equal/identical<br>
A **⊈** B: not a subset<br>
A **⊄** B: not a proper subset
</small>
]
]

## **Exercise VI: Stardew Valley Universe**
<br>
given the definitions to the right, **express** the meaning of the following sentences using **set theory**<br><br>
.pull-left[
1. Abigail is a villager.<br><br>
2. Mr. Qi does not live in Pelican Town.<br><br>
3. Every farmer grows crops.<br><br>
4. Some villagers raise chickens.<br><br>
5. Only one farmer lives in Pelican Town.<br><br>
6. Most villagers live in Pelican Town.<br><br>
7. Marnie and Shane both raise chickens.<br><br>
8. Neither Robin nor Abigail grow crops.
]
.pull-right[
[[Marnie]] = *m*<br>
[[Shane]] = *s*<br>
[[Mr. Qi]] = *q*<br>
[[Robin]] = *r*<br>
[[Abigail]] = *a*<br><br>
[[villager]] = { x | x is a villager } = *V*<br>
[[farmer]] = { x | x is a farmer } = *F*<br>
[[grow crops]] = { x | x grows crops } = *G*<br>
[[raise chickens]] = { x | x raises chickens } = *C*<br>
[[live in Pelican Town]] = { x | x lives in Pelican Town } = *P*
]
